title: Console-triggered on-demand row-encrypted CSV exports with ephemeral S3 URLs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a console-driven ad-hoc export flow allowing operators and customers (via Console UI) to request an immediate CSV snapshot for a tenant. Each CSV row must be encrypted at row-level using tenant-specific KMS keys; generated files are stored to S3 with short-lived presigned URLs (TTL 24 hours). The flow should integrate with existing export orchestration but bypass scheduled queues for manual runs, provide audit logs, and surface progress to Console. Key goals: minimize risk of plaintext PII exposure, ensure auditable triggers, and maintain existing SLAs for background scheduled exports.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI button to trigger ad-hoc export for a tenant (visible to appropriate roles)
Export job writes row-encrypted CSV(s) to customer-owned S3 bucket OR Redwood-managed bucket depending on tenancy
Presigned URLs generated with configurable TTL (default 24h) and returned in Console UI and audit log
Audit entry created with trigger user, timestamp, query parameters, and KMS key id
Job status visible in Console: Queued -> Running -> Completed/Failed with progress percent
Files are uploaded atomically (manifest + parts) and validated (checksum) before URL publication
Operations runbook added: manual cancel, retry, and key rotation impact notes
Security review completed and integration tests for KMS + presigned URL flow in CI
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-10 - Ava Chen: RFC draft posted (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/ad-hoc-exports-rfc). Proposed approach: reuse export-worker with a 'fast-path' flag to bypass scheduled throttles.
